title: VIX futures and options December 2027 expiration (SOQ settlement) — the December gap in this calendar's settlement series, filed on the OCC's own row with a SEVEN-DAY rule discrepancy recorded, not smoothed
source: EST: optionseducation.org/api/expirationcalendar, the OCC's own expiration calendar, fetched direct 2026-09-08 (HTTP 200, 34,871 bytes) by the fomc-minutes-2027-12-29 initial-research adjacency sweep. Its December 2027 rows, decoded against the file's own legend block, read verbatim: 2027-12-15 = 'Monthly Volatility Products Expiration date', 2027-12-16 = 'Monthly A.M. settled index options cease trading', 2027-12-17 = 'Monthly equity, index, and cash-settled currency options expiration date and PM settled index options cease trading', 2027-12-24 = 'Exchange/OCC holiday', 2027-12-31 = 'Quarterly Expiration date'. THE DISCREPANCY IS RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS LARGE AND THIS ENTRY DOES NOT RESOLVE IT. The standing rule -- the monthly VIX settlement is 30 days before the following month's monthly option expiration, itself the third Friday moved a day earlier when that Friday is a holiday -- reproduces the file for 34 of its 35 volatility rows, INCLUDING all three one-day cases, each explained by a holiday this session checked by name: 2025-03-18 (Good Friday 2025-04-18), 2026-05-19 (Juneteenth 2026-06-19) and 2027-05-18 (Juneteenth observed Friday 2027-06-18, since 2027-06-19 is a Saturday). The single failure is this row: the third Friday of January 2028 is 2028-01-21 with no holiday before it, so the rule gives Wednesday 2027-12-22 and the file gives 2027-12-15 -- a SEVEN-day gap, not a one-day adjustment, and the only such gap in the file. This entry follows the FILE, because the OCC is the primary and the rule is a reconstruction, but it is filed estimate on that discrepancy as well as on this lane's standing no-self-confirm limit for an event discovered in-sweep. Promotion requires re-reading a CBOE or OCC primary published closer to the date, not recomputing the rule. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: PROPOSED by the fomc-minutes-2027-12-29 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-08), at D-14 from that release on the file's date. LOAD-BEARING, not merely nearby. The fomc-minutes-2027-11-17 lane established the family's last surviving volatility statistic and then deflated it: VIX falls on 64.3% of 157 minutes releases, but split by whether the release shares its session with the monthly VIX settlement (both are Wednesdays, so 50 of 157 collide) it is 71.0% off-settlement against exactly 50.0% on-settlement, a 21.0pp gap at two-sided permutation p = 0.0122, with the collision half sitting exactly on the 54.4% universe base rate. Deciding which half 2027-12-29 falls in therefore requires knowing where December 2027's settlement is, and this calendar did not carry it: the vix-expiration series runs 2026-09-16, then 2027-01-20, 02-17, 03-17, 04-21, 05-18, 09-15, 10-20, 11-17 -- June, July, August and DECEMBER 2027 are all absent. THE SEVEN-DAY DISCREPANCY DOES NOT PROPAGATE INTO THE PROPOSER'S CONCLUSION, which is why this entry is safe to file while the discrepancy stands: 2027-12-29 is an OFF-settlement release under BOTH candidate dates (2027-12-15 and 2027-12-22), so no claim in fomc-minutes-2027-12-29.md turns on which is right. The proposing lane does not treat off-settlement status as support for anything either -- it measured the same headline a second way and found it is a calendar-window artifact on the December class: 18 of the 19 historical December-class releases land in the January 1-8 window, which runs 66.3% VIX-down on its own (n=95), and the releases add nothing over it (72.2%, P = 0.633). NOTHING TRADEABLE IS CLAIMED. symbols is empty and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is settlement-keyed. Proposed as an estimate; estimate widens caution and licenses no entry.
